title: The Best Indian Atheist Movies
description:
Indian cinema has repeatedly questioned blind faith. In this video we break down six films that put religion under a rational lens: Nirmalyam (Malayalam classic on temple decline), PK (satire on godmen and superstition), Naan Kadavul (Aghori life and fate vs agency), Prabhuvinte Makkal (a family’s clash over belief), Dasavatharam (history, sectarian conflict, reason), and Anbe Sivam (humanism over theism). We cover plots, themes, controversies and why these movies still matter.
Learn how filmmakers used satire, humanism and social critique to challenge ritual, miracle claims and religious authority.

 Nirmalyam (1973) — National Film Award; temple oracle story; Malayalam classic. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirmalyam
 PK (2014) — Religious satire; record-breaking box office; recurring controversy. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PK_(film)
 Anbe Sivam (2003) — Themes: humanism, atheism; cult classic over time. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anbe_Sivam
 Naan Kadavul (2009) — Aghori-centered drama exploring fate, religion, exploitation - https://www.theidolcast.com/postsbollywood/naan-kadavul-2009
 Dasavatharam (2008) — Historical opening on sectarian conflict; reason vs dogma thread. https://daminisreeraja.wordpress.com/2015/09/25/an-analysis-of-dasavatharams-opening-scene
 Prabhuvinte Makkal (2012) — Malayalam family drama around belief vs rationalism. https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8791998/
